question: The cutlery hand-off exists because the script says each item 'starts on the far side of the table from its target'. Is that true, and does removing the transfer place the cutlery?
row_under_test: req_demo_video (DRAFT) -- its stated blocker is task_success 0/10, whose largest missing component is cutlery placement

the_premise_is_false_on_reach.basis: envs/dinner_table.xml site and body positions, read from the shipped scene; distances are planar base-to-target
the_premise_is_false_on_reach.reading: Each picking arm is asked to reach a point 27-67 mm INSIDE the radius at which it already performs the pick on the same episode. Nothing about reach requires the transfer.
the_premise_is_false_on_reach.note: This refutes the stated PREMISE. It does not by itself say the transfer is harmful; the arms below measure that.

why_the_transfer_fails_prior_evidence_no.taker_reach.json: ik residual 1.6-7.7 mm at fork_take on all ten seeds; tracking error 61-303 mm
why_the_transfer_fails_prior_evidence_no.taker_servo.json: plan_err 43.9-46.5 mm on 10/10 (half the jaw opening); verdict BLOCKED_BY_GIVER on 6/10
why_the_transfer_fails_prior_evidence_no.fork_release.json: seeds_where_placer_ever_holds_the_fork EMPTY on all ten, against a positive control that sees the PICKER grasp on 9/10

method: Four arms, same 20 seeds, same scorer, same policy, privileged scene, --no-render. Paired per seed. Nothing in envs/task.py or the randomizer was touched.

knob_default_is_inert.how: With the knob unset, seeds 0 and 1 scored 3 and 2 -- identical to the pinned shipped column [3,2,3,1,1,1,1,2,2,2] -- both BEFORE the refactor and AFTER the knob was generalised to a set of body names. Run twice, /tmp/ctl_off.json and /tmp/ctl_off2.json.
knob_default_is_inert.why_it_matters: a knob whose OFF path has drifted is measuring a different robot

scorer_untouched.how: envs/task.py has no edit this tick; the same predicates score every arm

effect_is_localised.how: spoon_placed has ZERO discordant seeds between A and B even though B moves the spoon to direct place. An intervention that changed the score by disturbing the scorer would not leave a subgoal exactly invariant.
effect_is_localised.why_it_matters: NEGATIVE CONTROL -- it shows the gain is not a global shift

what_it_shows: The fork's failure was the TRANSFER. Direct place gains 6 seeds and loses 1 (exact p=0.125), 3/20 -> 8/20.

The spoon's failure is NOT the transfer. ZERO discordant seeds. evidence/spoon_depth.json already measured why: the spoon is never lifted more than 2.7-14.4 mm, so it is never in the giver's jaws for a transfer to fail.
Moving BOTH costs more than it collects: arm B loses drawer_open on 2 seeds to the crossing arm and scores the same 35/100 as arm C, which loses 1.
Arm C is the first controller change in this workspace to beat the shipped column on the aggregate: 35/100 vs 32/100, better on 8 seeds and worse on 4.
what_it_does_NOT_show: It does not show a significant aggregate gain. The paired sign test on arm C is p=0.388 and on arm B is p=1.000. At n=20 neither clears any conventional bar.
It does not show task success. task_success is 0/20 in every arm, so req_demo_video does NOT become READY on this measurement.
The fork target metric itself is p=0.125, which is a direction, not a proof.

It does not measure the RUBRIC cost. T1 names 'object hand-off' among what it scores, and arm C stops producing fork hand-off events (A recorded 3 fork + 1 spoon over 20 seeds; C records 0 cutlery hand-offs). Whether 5 extra fork placements outweigh that on a 30-point criterion is a judging question this measurement cannot answer.
adoption: NOT ADOPTED. CUTLERY_DIRECT_PLACE ships at none. Arm C was adopted mid-tick and REVERTED inside the same tick; the tree is byte-restored.
adoption_reasoning: Arm C is the better arm and this file's own numbers say so. It is not shipped because adopting it restates far more than the two artifacts I had planned to regenerate, and I found that by trying it rather than by reasoning about it. The controller is the shared denominator of three OTHER published arms -- eval_seeds_scripted_perceived.json, the blind negative control, and eval_seeds_act.json, which quotes the ACT policy as '3/50 against the scripted controller's 18/50' -- and of four artifacts generated out of evidence/ (cover image, slides, video presentation, demo site), each with a controls file that machine-checks its claims against evidence and would correctly go red on a partial adoption. A half-reconciled tree publishes claims its own code no longer produces, which is worse than an unadopted improvement.
